title: Deuteronomy Chapter 26 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Deuteronomy chapter 26 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 26 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Deuteronomy Chapter 26.

questions.question: When you come into the land that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance, what must you do with the first of all the fruit of the earth?
options: Put it in a basket and bring it to the place God chooses to place His name
Eat it immediately
Sell it to the Levites
Burn it as an offering
questions.correctAnswer: Put it in a basket and bring it to the place God chooses to place His name
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:2 instructs to take the first of all the fruit, put it in a basket, and go to the place the LORD will choose to place His name.

questions.question: To whom must you present the basket of firstfruits when you come to the chosen place?
options: The priest
The king
The prophet
The Levite
questions.correctAnswer: The priest
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:3 says you must go to the priest and say the required confession.

questions.question: What does the priest do with the basket of firstfruits when you give it to him?
options: Takes it and sets it down before the altar of the LORD
Gives it back to you
Distributes it among the people
Burns it as a sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: Takes it and sets it down before the altar of the LORD
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:4 states the priest takes the basket and sets it down before the altar of the LORD.

questions.question: In the confession spoken before the LORD, how is the father described?
options: A Syrian ready to perish
A mighty king
A priest in Egypt
A wandering Levite
questions.correctAnswer: A Syrian ready to perish
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:5 describes the father as a Syrian ready to perish who went down to Egypt.

questions.question: How did the Egyptians treat the Israelites according to the confession?
options: They evil entreated and afflicted them, laying hard bondage upon them
They welcomed them as friends
They ignored them
They gave them land to dwell in
questions.correctAnswer: They evil entreated and afflicted them, laying hard bondage upon them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:6 states that the Egyptians evil entreated and afflicted Israel and laid hard bondage upon them.

questions.question: What did the LORD do when the Israelites cried out because of their affliction?
options: He heard their voice and looked on their affliction, labor, and oppression
He ignored their cries
He sent prophets to warn them
He punished them further
questions.correctAnswer: He heard their voice and looked on their affliction, labor, and oppression
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:7 explains that when Israel cried to the LORD, He heard their voice and looked on their affliction.

questions.question: True or False: You must rejoice before the LORD with your household, including the Levite and the stranger.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:11 commands rejoicing in every good thing given by the LORD, including with the Levite and stranger.

questions.question: True or False: The third year is called the year of tithing when you give the tithes to the Levite, stranger, fatherless, and widow.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:12 refers to the third year as the year of tithing when tithes are given to the Levite and others.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 26, it is permitted to eat the hallowed things in mourning.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:14 states that one must not eat the hallowed things in mourning or use them for unclean purposes.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD promises to make Israel high above all nations in praise, name, and honor.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:19 assures that the LORD will make Israel high above all nations in praise, name, and honor.

questions.question: What must you say before the LORD after giving the tithes according to His commandments?
options: I have brought away the hallowed things and given them as commanded; I have not transgressed nor forgotten Thy commandments
I have kept all the gold for myself
I have given nothing to the Levite
I have forgotten Thy commandments
questions.correctAnswer: I have brought away the hallowed things and given them as commanded; I have not transgressed nor forgotten Thy commandments
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:13 contains this confession after giving the tithes according to God's commandments.

questions.question: What does the LORD command you to do with all your heart and soul on this day?
options: Keep and do His statutes and judgments
Forget the commandments
Follow your own ways
Ignore His voice
questions.correctAnswer: Keep and do His statutes and judgments
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:16 commands obedience to the statutes and judgments with all heart and soul.

questions.question: Who has the LORD avouched to be His peculiar people as promised?
options: Israel
Egyptians
Syrians
Canaanites
questions.correctAnswer: Israel
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:18 states that the LORD has avouched Israel to be His peculiar people as promised.

questions.question: What is the reason given for bringing the firstfruits to the LORD?
options: Because the LORD has given you the land flowing with milk and honey
To gain wealth
To impress the priest
To show off your harvest
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD has given you the land flowing with milk and honey
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:9-10 explains the LORD brought Israel to a land flowing with milk and honey, and the firstfruits are brought as acknowledgment.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 26, which instruction comes first?
options: Take the firstfruits and bring them in a basket to the chosen place
Give tithes to the Levite and stranger
Rejoice with your household
Say the confession after giving tithes
questions.correctAnswer: Take the firstfruits and bring them in a basket to the chosen place
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:1-2 begins the chapter with the instruction to take the firstfruits and bring them to the place the LORD chooses.

medium.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 26 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Deuteronomy Chapter 26 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 26:8, how did the LORD bring the Israelites out of Egypt?
options: With a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, great terribleness, signs, and wonders
With gentle guidance and peaceful ways
By sending angels to lead them
Through secret paths and quiet miracles
questions.correctAnswer: With a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, great terribleness, signs, and wonders
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:8 explicitly states that the LORD brought the Israelites out of Egypt with a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, great terribleness, and with signs and wonders, demonstrating God's powerful intervention.

questions.question: What is described in Deuteronomy 26:9 as the land God gave to the Israelites?
options: A land that floweth with milk and honey
A desert full of challenges
A mountainous territory with few resources
A land of endless rivers
questions.correctAnswer: A land that floweth with milk and honey
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:9 describes the land God gave as one that 'floweth with milk and honey,' symbolizing abundance and blessing.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 26:10, what should a person do after bringing the firstfruits of the land?
options: Set it before the LORD and worship Him
Eat it alone in private
Sell it to neighbors
Offer it to the king
questions.correctAnswer: Set it before the LORD and worship Him
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:10 instructs to set the firstfruits before the LORD and worship Him, showing gratitude for God's provision.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 26:11 teach about rejoicing in God's blessings?
options: By rejoicing in every good thing given to you, your household, the Levite, and the stranger
By keeping blessings secret and personal
By donating all to the temple only
By fasting after receiving blessings
questions.correctAnswer: By rejoicing in every good thing given to you, your household, the Levite, and the stranger
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:11 encourages rejoicing in God's blessings not just for oneself but also for one's household, the Levite, and the stranger, emphasizing communal joy and gratitude.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 26:12, who should receive the tithes during the year of tithing?
options: The Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
Only the priests
The king and his officials
The wealthy landowners
questions.correctAnswer: The Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:12 specifies that tithes are to be given to the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow so they may be satisfied within the gates.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 26:13 require the giver to declare after giving tithes?
options: That they have obeyed the commandments and not forgotten them
That they gave reluctantly and with complaints
That they expect something in return
That they gave secretly without telling anyone
questions.correctAnswer: That they have obeyed the commandments and not forgotten them
questions.explanation: In verse 13, the giver must confess before the LORD that they have not transgressed or forgotten God's commandments, highlighting integrity and obedience in giving.

questions.question: Deuteronomy 26:14 teaches that one must not do which of the following with the tithes?
options: Eat it in mourning or use it for unclean purposes
Share it generously with neighbors
Offer it gladly to the LORD
Keep it for future needs
questions.correctAnswer: Eat it in mourning or use it for unclean purposes
questions.explanation: Verse 14 forbids eating the tithes in mourning or using them for any unclean use or for the dead, emphasizing purity and respect for God's commands.

questions.question: What is the significance of the declaration in Deuteronomy 26:15?
options: A prayer for God to bless Israel and the land as promised
A request for personal wealth and success
A vow to build a temple
An announcement of war against enemies
questions.correctAnswer: A prayer for God to bless Israel and the land as promised
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:15 is a prayer asking God to look down from heaven and bless Israel and the land as He swore to the ancestors, underscoring reliance on God's faithful promises.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 26:16, what attitude should one have when keeping God's statutes and judgments?
options: With all heart and soul
Halfheartedly and occasionally
Only when convenient
Out of fear of punishment
questions.correctAnswer: With all heart and soul
questions.explanation: Verse 16 instructs that the statutes and judgments should be kept with all one's heart and soul, implying full devotion and commitment.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 26:17 say the Israelites have done on this day regarding the LORD?
options: Avouched the LORD to be their God and vowed to walk in His ways
Rejected the LORD's commandments
Made a covenant with foreign gods
Decided to follow only some laws
questions.correctAnswer: Avouched the LORD to be their God and vowed to walk in His ways
questions.explanation: According to verse 17, the Israelites publicly declared the LORD as their God and committed to walking in His ways, obeying statutes and commandments.

questions.question: What promise does the LORD make to Israel in Deuteronomy 26:18?
options: That they will be His peculiar people if they keep His commandments
That they will never face hardship
That they will conquer all nations immediately
That they will have riches without obedience
questions.correctAnswer: That they will be His peculiar people if they keep His commandments
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states that God has claimed Israel as His special people, contingent upon their obedience to His commandments.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 26:19 describe the status God will give Israel if they obey Him?
options: High above all nations in praise, name, and honor
Hidden among the nations without distinction
Equal to all nations without special status
Oppressed by other nations
questions.correctAnswer: High above all nations in praise, name, and honor
questions.explanation: Verse 19 promises Israel will be exalted above all nations in praise, name, and honor, becoming a holy people unto the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 26:13 requires the giver to admit forgetting some of God's commandments.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:13 says the giver declares they have not transgressed or forgotten God's commandments, affirming obedience and remembrance.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 26:14 teaches that tithes must not be eaten during mourning or used for unclean purposes.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 14 explicitly states tithes should not be eaten in mourning nor taken for any unclean use, underscoring reverence and purity.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 26:12, tithes are meant only for the Levites and no one else.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 12 specifies that tithes are for the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow, showing God’s concern for vulnerable groups.

hard.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 26 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Deuteronomy Chapter 26.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 26:15, what does Israel ask God to do from His holy habitation?
options: Look down and bless His people Israel and the land He gave them
Send fire from heaven to consume their enemies
Forget their past sins and renew their covenant
Grant them victory over all nations immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Look down and bless His people Israel and the land He gave them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:15 specifically petitions God to look down from heaven and bless His people Israel and the land given to them, as He swore to their fathers.

questions.question: What is commanded in Deuteronomy 26:16 regarding statutes and judgments?
options: To keep and do them with all heart and soul
To teach them only to the priests
To write them on stones at the city gates
To follow them only during festivals
questions.correctAnswer: To keep and do them with all heart and soul
questions.explanation: Verse 16 commands the people to keep and do the statutes and judgments with all their heart and soul, emphasizing wholehearted obedience.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 26:17, what has Israel avouched the LORD to be?
options: Their God to walk in His ways and keep His commandments
A distant judge watching from afar
A God only for the priests and Levites
A warrior who fights their battles automatically
questions.correctAnswer: Their God to walk in His ways and keep His commandments
questions.explanation: The verse makes clear that Israel avouches the LORD as their God and commits to walk in His ways and obey His commandments.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 26:18, what status does the LORD confer upon Israel?
options: His peculiar people as He promised
A nation like all others without distinction
A conquered people under foreign rule
His servants only during the festival season
questions.correctAnswer: His peculiar people as He promised
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states that the LORD hath avouched Israel to be His peculiar people, fulfilling His promise conditional on their obedience.

questions.question: What is the purpose of making Israel 'high above all nations' in Deuteronomy 26:19?
options: To be holy and honored before the LORD
To dominate militarily over neighbors
To accumulate wealth and land
To enforce their laws on other nations
questions.correctAnswer: To be holy and honored before the LORD
questions.explanation: The verse explains the elevation is for praise, name, and honor so Israel may be a holy people unto the LORD, reflecting a spiritual distinction rather than mere political dominance.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God blessing His people and land as in Deuteronomy 26:15?
options: Psalm 67:1
Genesis 1:1
Exodus 3:14
Revelation 21:1
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 67:1
questions.explanation: Psalm 67:1 similarly asks God to be gracious and bless His people, making His face shine upon them, echoing the blessing request in Deuteronomy 26:15.

questions.question: What Hebrew word is translated as 'peculiar people' in Deuteronomy 26:18, and what does it imply?
options: Am Segulah, meaning a treasured or special possession
Nephesh, meaning soul or life
Chesed, meaning lovingkindness
Ruach, meaning spirit or breath
questions.correctAnswer: Am Segulah, meaning a treasured or special possession
questions.explanation: 'Am Segulah' is the Hebrew term used in verse 18, denoting Israel as God's treasured possession, highlighting their special covenant relationship.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in the narrative of Deuteronomy 26:5-10 regarding the history of Israel?
options: Inclusio, framing the narrative with the firstfruits offering
Metaphor, comparing Israel to a lion
Allegory, representing Egypt as a beast
Hyperbole, exaggerating the affliction in Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio, framing the narrative with the firstfruits offering
questions.explanation: Verses 5-10 use an inclusio literary device, starting and ending with the offering of firstfruits to frame Israel’s history from affliction in Egypt to receiving the promised land.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 26:12, who are the recipients of the tithes given during the year of tithing?
options: The Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
Only the priests in the temple
The king and his officials
The elders of the city
questions.correctAnswer: The Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
questions.explanation: Verse 12 clearly states the tithes are given to those groups so they may eat and be filled within the gates, reflecting social justice concerns.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 26:14, what is specifically forbidden concerning the hallowed things?
options: Eating them in mourning or giving them for unclean or dead uses
Selling them for profit
Sharing them only with family
Using them to bribe officials
questions.correctAnswer: Eating them in mourning or giving them for unclean or dead uses
questions.explanation: The verse forbids eating the hallowed things in mourning, using them for unclean purposes, or giving them for the dead, emphasizing proper sanctity and use.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 26:16 commands Israel to obey God's statutes and judgments with partial commitment.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:16 requires obedience with all heart and all soul, indicating full commitment rather than partial obedience.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 26:19 states that Israel shall be made high above all nations for the purpose of being an holy people unto the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 19 explicitly says Israel will be exalted above all nations to be holy before the LORD, affirming their special status and calling.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 26:8 describe the manner in which the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt?
options: With a mighty hand, outstretched arm, great terribleness, signs, and wonders
By sending a gentle wind to part the sea
Through secret paths unknown to the Egyptians
By negotiating a peaceful treaty
questions.correctAnswer: With a mighty hand, outstretched arm, great terribleness, signs, and wonders
questions.explanation: Verse 8 vividly describes the powerful and awe-inspiring nature of Israel's deliverance from Egypt.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of dedicating firstfruits to God as found in Deuteronomy 26:2-10?
options: Romans 8:23
John 3:16
Acts 2:38
Hebrews 11:1
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 8:23
questions.explanation: Romans 8:23 speaks of believers having the firstfruits of the Spirit, echoing the Old Testament concept of firstfruits dedication in Deuteronomy 26.

questions.question: What historical context is reflected in Deuteronomy 26:6-7 regarding Israel's experience in Egypt?
options: Harsh bondage and affliction by Egyptians
Peaceful cohabitation and trade
Political alliance and marriage
Warfare between Israel and Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Harsh bondage and affliction by Egyptians
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 recount the severe oppression and hard bondage Israel suffered in Egypt before God's deliverance.

theological.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 26 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Deuteronomy Chapter 26 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What specific act does Deuteronomy 26:2 command the Israelites to perform when they enter the land given by God?
options: Bring the first fruits of the land in a basket to the place God will choose
Offer a burnt sacrifice upon entering the land
Build an altar on every high hill
Write God's commandments on the doorposts of their houses
questions.correctAnswer: Bring the first fruits of the land in a basket to the place God will choose
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:2 instructs the Israelites to take the first fruits of all the fruit of the earth and bring them in a basket to the place the LORD will choose to place His name. This act symbolizes acknowledging God's provision and ownership over the land.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 26:5, which historical narrative does the speaker recount to the priest when presenting the first fruits?
options: The story of their father as a Syrian ready to perish who went down into Egypt and became a great nation
The Exodus from Babylonian captivity
The conquest of Canaan under Joshua
The giving of the Law at Mount Sinai
questions.correctAnswer: The story of their father as a Syrian ready to perish who went down into Egypt and became a great nation
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:5 recounts the ancestral history of the Israelites, beginning with a 'Syrian ready to perish' (Jacob) who went down into Egypt and whose descendants became a populous nation, emphasizing God's providential care and faithfulness.

questions.question: What divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Deuteronomy 26:8 by the description of God's deliverance from Egypt?
options: Omnipotence, shown by the mighty hand and outstretched arm
Immutability, shown by unchanging laws
Omniscience, shown by foreknowledge of events
Justice, shown by punishing the Egyptians
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence, shown by the mighty hand and outstretched arm
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:8 highlights God's omnipotence through the mighty hand and outstretched arm used to bring Israel out of Egypt with great signs and wonders. This reveals God's supreme power in salvation.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 26:11 expand the scope of rejoicing beyond the individual Israelite?
options: It includes the entire household, the Levite, and the stranger among them
It restricts rejoicing to the priests only
It commands rejoicing only in the temple during festivals
It limits rejoicing to the elders of the community
questions.correctAnswer: It includes the entire household, the Levite, and the stranger among them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:11 commands rejoicing in every good thing given by God, not only by the individual but also by their household, the Levite (the priestly tribe), and the stranger living among them, emphasizing communal joy and inclusion.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by the instructions in Deuteronomy 26:12-13 concerning tithing and giving to the Levite, stranger, fatherless, and widow?
options: The doctrine of social holiness and covenantal obedience
The doctrine of justification by faith alone
The doctrine of predestination
The doctrine of original sin
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of social holiness and covenantal obedience
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:12-13 teaches the obligation to support the marginalized within the community, such as the Levite and the vulnerable, demonstrating social holiness—the call to live out covenant obedience in practical care for others.

questions.question: What combined theological truth do Deuteronomy 26:16 and 26:17 teach about the believer's relationship to God's statutes?
options: Believers must keep God's statutes wholeheartedly as a covenantal commitment to walk in His ways
Believers are only required to keep the statutes when convenient
Believers may selectively obey statutes based on personal judgment
Believers are freed from the obligation to obey statutes after entering the land
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must keep God's statutes wholeheartedly as a covenantal commitment to walk in His ways
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:16-17 emphasize that the LORD commands obedience to statutes and judgments with all heart and soul, and that Israel avouches God as their God to walk in His ways, showing covenant commitment and wholehearted obedience.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 26:18-19, what special status does God confer upon Israel for keeping His commandments?
options: They become His peculiar people, exalted above all nations in praise, name, and honor
They become rulers over all other gods
They are exempt from all future judgment
They receive automatic material blessings without obedience
questions.correctAnswer: They become His peculiar people, exalted above all nations in praise, name, and honor
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:18-19 states that God avouches Israel to be His peculiar people and will make them high above all nations in praise, name, and honor if they keep His commandments, signifying their covenant identity and divine election.

questions.question: What theological synthesis emerges from comparing Deuteronomy 26:6 and 26:7 about God's response to Israel's suffering in Egypt?
options: God is compassionate and responsive to the cries of His oppressed people
God is indifferent to human suffering
Human suffering is unrelated to God's actions
God punishes the innocent for the sins of their ancestors
questions.correctAnswer: God is compassionate and responsive to the cries of His oppressed people
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:6-7 portrays God hearing Israel's cries amid affliction and oppression and responding with deliverance, revealing His compassionate and responsive nature toward His people’s suffering.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 26:14 clarify the sanctity required in handling the tithes and offerings?
options: The tithes must not be eaten in mourning or used for unclean purposes or for the dead
The tithes can be used for any purpose after collection
The tithes are to be kept secret from the community
The tithes are optional and may be disregarded
questions.correctAnswer: The tithes must not be eaten in mourning or used for unclean purposes or for the dead
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:14 commands that the tithes must be handled reverently—not eaten during mourning, nor used for unclean purposes, nor given for the dead—indicating the holiness and purity required in worship practices.

questions.question: What does the expression 'a land that floweth with milk and honey' in Deuteronomy 26:9 signify about God's provision?
options: It symbolizes abundance, blessing, and the fulfillment of God's promise
It indicates harsh and barren conditions
It refers to a land cursed by God
It describes a land to be conquered with great difficulty
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes abundance, blessing, and the fulfillment of God's promise
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:9 describes the land given by God as one flowing with milk and honey, which symbolizes abundant provision, blessing, and the fulfillment of God's covenant promise to Israel.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that ancient laws like those in Deuteronomy 26 promote legalism rather than genuine worship. What does Deuteronomy 26:10-11 teach about the nature of worship in relation to God's gifts?
options: Worship involves joyful thanksgiving and recognition of God's gifts, not mere legal obligation
Worship is solely about ritual sacrifice without personal joy
Worship is an empty formality with no heart involvement
Worship requires isolation and exclusion of others
questions.correctAnswer: Worship involves joyful thanksgiving and recognition of God's gifts, not mere legal obligation
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:10-11 connects the presentation of first fruits with worship and rejoicing in God's blessings, demonstrating that true worship includes heartfelt gratitude and communal joy, countering claims of mere legalism.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted in Deuteronomy 26:15 where the people ask God to look down from heaven and bless them as He swore to their fathers?
options: Faithfulness to His covenant promises
Impersonality and distance from creation
Indifference to human affairs
Injustice toward the nations
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness to His covenant promises
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:15 shows the people appealing to God's faithfulness, asking Him to bless the land as He swore to their fathers, thereby emphasizing God's unwavering commitment to His covenant promises.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 26:4 reveal about the role of the priest in the ritual of presenting first fruits?
options: The priest takes the basket and places it before the altar of the LORD
The priest offers a burnt offering in place of the people
The priest distributes the first fruits among the people
The priest judges the worthiness of the fruits
questions.correctAnswer: The priest takes the basket and places it before the altar of the LORD
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:4 outlines the priest's role as receiving the basket from the worshiper and setting it down before the altar, signifying mediation between the people and God in worship.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight is conveyed by Deuteronomy 26:1 and 26:19 regarding God's gift and Israel's calling?
options: God gives the land as an inheritance and calls Israel to be a holy people exalted above all nations
Israel earns the land by their own merit and is to remain separate and isolated
The land is a temporary possession with no covenantal significance
Israel's calling is independent of God's gift of the land
questions.correctAnswer: God gives the land as an inheritance and calls Israel to be a holy people exalted above all nations
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:1 introduces the land as an inheritance given by God, and verse 26:19 speaks of Israel’s exaltation and holiness because of covenant obedience, teaching that the land and calling are gifts from God tied to holiness.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 26:13 express the believer's affirmation of obedience and remembrance of God's commandments?
options: By declaring they have not transgressed or forgotten God's commandments in giving to the needy
By confessing frequent disobedience and neglect
By claiming exemption from certain commandments
By delegating obedience to the Levites alone
questions.correctAnswer: By declaring they have not transgressed or forgotten God's commandments in giving to the needy
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 26:13 requires the speaker to affirm that they have faithfully obeyed God's commandments, especially in giving to the Levite, stranger, fatherless, and widow, demonstrating covenant faithfulness and remembrance.
